Hi Tom,

Thanks again for taking the time today — good discussion. Below is a short recap of what I heard and the specific items we'd like to validate so we can size a proof-of-concept and put together an indicative pricing/commit sheet. If anything below doesn't match your view, please flag.

Recap (high level):
- Primary app: patient intake + clinician summarization pipeline (real-time assistant embedded in web UI).
- Target peak concurrency: ~1,000 concurrent users (typical active generation per user).
- Expected steady throughput: 60–80 requests/sec, with bursts to ~120 rps for short windows.
- Latency goal (customer SLO request): p95 <= 250ms for non-streamed completions, and first-byte <= 120ms for streaming responses.
- Response size: typical output 512–2,048 tokens; worst-case long summaries up to ~8,000 tokens.
- Input context: average 1,000 tokens; some sessions will send rolling conversation history + documents up to 24k tokens.
- Requirement: streaming partial results into the UI (progressive summaries) and graceful fallback to shorter outputs when latency/throughput constraints hit limits.

Clarification asks (items we promised to confirm):
1) For the long-context flows, do you need the entire 24k input to be used for every generation, or can the UI send a trimmed context (e.g., last 6k tokens + retrieved docs) for low-latency paths?
2) For the 8k-token outputs, how common are those (est % of traffic)? This affects batching and KV-cache sizing.
3) Are there any strict network egress constraints (private peering only) or can we use our hosted endpoints in us-east-1 for the POC?

Next steps I propose:
- Vivek and Laura to propose two SLO/throughput configurations (latency-optimized and cost-optimized) with recommended model families and quantization profiles.
- We'll provide a simple POC plan: 72-hour run with synthetic load + a small integration test using a subset of your anonymized conversation logs.
- Procurement: Tom to introduce procurement@luminacare.io if procurement needs a statement of work / security questionnaire.

Attached: preliminary SLO matrix draft and a short network latency capture you mentioned in the call.

Can you confirm answers to the clarifying questions above? If it helps, we can also schedule a 30-min technical deep-dive next week.

Best,

Tom / Marissa — quick technical follow-up from my side after the call. Repeating Marissa's key bullets for context.

On 2027-04-11 Marissa Cole wrote:
> - Target peak concurrency: ~1,000 concurrent users
> - Throughput bursts to ~120 rps
> - p95 <= 250ms non-streamed; first-byte <= 120ms streamed
> - Inputs: up to 24k tokens in some sessions; outputs up to 8k tokens worst case

A few notes and engineering constraints to consider:
1) Model selection and KV cache: if you want the full 24k context to be available for every generation, that pushes us to model variants and execution paths that hold larger KV caches per connection — this increases memory pressure and can limit effective batching (reduces tokens/sec per GPU).
2) Streaming trade-off: First-byte <=120ms is achievable with smaller initial decoding windows and prefix caching, but for large outputs (multi-thousand tokens) the overall completion time will still be dominated by decode time — we can stream early tokens fast but tail latency for full 8k outputs will be minutes unless we accept lower sampling temperature / constrained max tokens or run on higher-compute families.
3) Concurrency shaping: to hold p95 250ms at 1,000 concurrent users we may need to partition traffic across multiple dedicated pools (or rely on burst capacity). That also affects cost profile — I've sketched two capacity profiles in the attached SLO matrix.

Questions for LuminaCare: can you provide: (a) an estimate of % of sessions that will require a full-document 24k context vs those that only require trimmed histories, (b) whether you control the client-side UX to implement partial-context fallbacks (recommended).

I'll prepare two concrete configs tonight:
- Latency-first: smaller models, more parallel replicas, aggressive prefix caching; target p95 <= 250ms for outputs up to 2k tokens, degrade gracefully for longer outputs.
- Throughput-first: larger batch sizes, quantized models, higher token throughput with p95 ~350–450ms for 2–4k outputs, but much lower $/token.

—Vivek

Tom — following up with a concrete SLO matrix and initial sizing assumptions (attached). Summary below.

SLO profiles (summary):
- Profile A (latency-optimized): p95 <= 250ms for outputs <= 2k tokens, streaming first-byte <= 100ms. Recommended: 8x A100-equivalent GPUs reserved, model family: redwood-l/rt-13b (quant int8) for staging POC. Estimated steady cost: $X/hr (see attached).
- Profile B (cost-optimized): p95 <= 400ms for outputs <= 4k tokens, streaming first-byte <= 200ms. Recommended: 4x A100-equivalent GPUs, model family: redwood-s/rt-30b (quant int4). Use sharded KV caching and aggressive batching.

Context window handling:
- For sessions with >8k combined (input+expected output) we recommend a hybrid approach: client-side trimming to last 4–6k tokens + document retrieval (embedding-based) and only include the most relevant document slices in the prompt. We can also provide an infra-managed prefix cache for recent context to speed repeated short-turns.

POC proposal: 72-hour run; we run synthetic ramp to your provided concurrency shape and an integration test that replays a 1% sample of your anonymized logs. Deliverables: latency/throughput report, per-token cost estimates, and a short ops runbook for failover.

Procurement / security checklist: if procurement prefers a single SOW, we can send an MSFT SOW + SOC2 evidence pack. Marissa — Tom asked about an on-prem option; we can include a Private deployment quote in parallel but that extends procurement lead time.

I attached: LuminaCare_SLO_matrix_v1.xlsx (detailed cost/SLO table) and network_latency_summary.png that Marissa uploaded.

Next steps:
- Tom to confirm: (1) % of sessions needing full 24k context, (2) willingness to implement client-side trimming for latency-critical flows, (3) procurement contact info if they want a formal SOW.
- We will deliver an estimated POC price and a limited-time test account (sandbox) so LuminaCare can do an integration smoke test.

Thanks — Laura

Marissa / team — thanks, that write-up is super helpful and lines up with what we discussed. Quick answers below:

1) Full 24k context usage: rare — ~5% of sessions. Most (~80%) will be short histories <2k tokens. The heavy contexts are for weekly multi-document reviews from clinicians.
2) 8k-token outputs: infrequent — estimate ~3–5% of traffic; most outputs are 512–1,500 tokens.
3) Networking: POC can use hosted endpoints in us-east-1. For production we will likely require VPC peering (security team).

Procurement: forwarding to procurement@luminacare.io — please send an SOW + indicative POC pricing and any SOC2 docs. Also, we'd like access to a sandbox/test account for a short integration smoke test ahead of the POC.

Next steps from our side:
- Procurement will confirm SOW requirements and contract owners by EOD Friday.
- I'll also share a small anonymized sample of long-context sessions for you to run through the sizing exercise (will target <500MB).

Appreciate the two profile options — please send the POC estimate + sandbox credentials and we'll triage with procurement. Happy to do a 30-min tech call next week if needed (Wed/Thu mornings ET work best).

Best,
Tom Hayes
